evidence.exact_quote: OpenCode is **server-bridged only**. Puppet Master MUST communicate via HTTP REST + SSE through the unified Provider facade; it MUST NOT run OpenCode as a CLI-bridged runtime transport.

items.impact: This locks the transport authority and prevents a builder from treating the CLI launcher fallback as the runtime protocol.
items.statement: OpenCode runtime calls are exclusively HTTP REST plus SSE through the unified Provider facade; CLI use is restricted to discovery or managed launch support.
items.title: Server-bridged transport is explicitly authoritative

evidence.exact_quote: OpenCode request dispatch is queue-backed and provider-account scoped.
OpenCode still exposes transport platform/model without clear ownership of upstream provider/account identity.

items.impact: Independent implementations can key the same OpenCode server-profile queue by PM account, upstream account, or server profile, producing over-serialization, rate-limit bypass, or cross-tenant interference.
items.statement: The prose declares provider-account-scoped dispatch while also acknowledging that upstream provider/account ownership is unclear; it never defines the canonical queue/concurrency key for a server profile exposing multiple upstream providers or accounts.
items.title: Concurrency scope lacks a canonical identity key

evidence.exact_quote: OpenCode server routes, OpenCode/Models.dev provider catalogs, `opencode-cursor`, `opencode-gpt-imagegen`, and current OpenCode coding-plan config are source-lineage or OpenCode-provider evidence unless the target provider route is explicitly OpenCode server.

items.impact: The boundary prevents OpenCode catalogs and unofficial plugins from being mistaken for PM-owned direct-provider readiness or canonical media backends.
items.statement: PO-048 cleanly confines OpenCode and Models.dev mappings to source-lineage evidence unless the implemented route is explicitly the OpenCode server route.
items.title: OpenCode source-lineage evidence is not direct-provider closure

evidence.exact_quote: attempt reconnect when `auto_retry_stream: true` (default)
OpenCode transport reconnect logic may reconnect only to observe an existing attempt; it MUST NOT silently resubmit prompts, reset attempt identity, or invent provider-local fallback loops

items.impact: A builder can interpret reconnect as prompt resubmission with partial context or as observation-only reconnection; the first risks duplicate mutations and the second may be impossible without a specified resume cursor.
items.statement: The core first specifies adapter-owned automatic stream retry with partial-response continuation, then supersedes local retry wording and permits reconnection only to observe the existing attempt, without defining an observation/resume API or precedence rule.
items.title: Streaming recovery contradicts canonical retry ownership

evidence.exact_quote: OpenCode is server-bridged only: Puppet Master communicates through HTTP REST plus SSE via the unified Provider facade and must not run OpenCode as a CLI-bridged runtime transport.

items.impact: The PlanUnits preserve the transport, PM-native vocabulary, identity, profile, discovery, and stale-status boundaries as separately addressable requirements.
items.statement: PO-002 through PO-008 atomize the principal OpenCode transport, terminology, identity, profile, readiness, and GUI stale-state contracts, while the PO-048 continuation preserves its source-lineage boundary.
items.title: Core OpenCode boundaries are addressable PlanUnits

evidence.exact_quote: Server-Bridged Transport Authority remains addressable as a fine-grained Provider OpenCode PlanUnit.

items.impact: Index and migration validators can pass while transport denial, identity preservation, state transitions, and stale GUI behavior remain unimplemented or incorrect.
items.statement: The PlanUnits' acceptance criteria test addressability and lineage preservation rather than their stated product behavior; the validation surfaces are plan-index and migration checks, not executable provider or GUI oracles.
items.title: PlanUnit acceptance criteria do not falsify product behavior

evidence.exact_quote: OpenCode has separate server-level auth and provider-level auth realms: PM sends configured server credentials to OpenCode endpoints and treats upstream provider auth as OpenCode-managed provider-native auth exposed by /provider/auth and callback endpoints.

items.impact: The split prevents server credentials, upstream provider auth, PM lineage, and provider-native session/cache identifiers from collapsing into one authority or persistence domain.
items.statement: The auth, envelope, discovered-provider, cache-metadata, and session-to-run PlanUnits consistently preserve PM authority while treating OpenCode identities and state as additive provider evidence.
items.title: PM and OpenCode authority domains remain distinct

evidence.exact_quote: records server version from health checks, and emits version_mismatch diagnostics when required while continuing best-effort operation.

items.impact: An incompatible server may remain selectable and fail later in a less diagnosable path, or builders may disable different features for the same version mismatch.
items.statement: PO-010 requires best-effort continuation after version mismatch but does not map minimum versions to affected capabilities, define hard-stop conditions, or specify effective-capability downgrades.
items.title: Version mismatch has no capability gating contract

evidence.exact_quote: keeps last-known connected upstream models visible until refresh finishes, and reports progress or per-provider failure in the shell /status-bar without blocking runtime selection.

items.impact: A user can select a stale model whose provider auth or availability has changed, yet the plan does not define warning, preflight, rollback, or blocked-state behavior for the resulting run.
items.statement: PO-013 deliberately leaves runtime selection unblocked during background refresh but specifies only status-bar reporting, not the execution semantics of choosing stale last-known provider/model/auth facts.
items.title: Boot refresh permits stale selection without a run-time contract

evidence.exact_quote: OpenCode response parts and SSE bus events map into PM normalized provider events for text_delta, thinking_delta, tool_use, tool_result, usage, error, and done, with PM subscribing to GET /event after prompt_async and emitting done when the session reaches completed or failed.
GET /event → SSE stream

items.impact: Subscribing after prompt submission can lose fast session events or completion, while subscribing before submission requires a correlation/filtering contract for the server-global stream; builders cannot satisfy both sequences.
items.statement: PO-016 says to subscribe to GET /event after prompt_async, contradicting the normative invocation sequence that subscribes before sending prompt_async; neither statement defines a cursor or replay boundary.
items.title: SSE subscription order is contradictory and race-prone

evidence.exact_quote: OpenCode-specific adapter behavior preserves PM requested/effective runtime and capability disclosure, keeps provider-native agent files and invocation syntax in the interoperability lane, supports additive provider correlation, preserves prompt-cache separation, avoids fake-user replay continuity, and keeps Copilot-sensitive billing/classification metadata from weakening PM strict-deny policy.

items.impact: These constraints keep provider-native features and billing metadata from bypassing PM policy, capability, and usage ownership.
items.statement: The auth, adapter-policy, discovery, picker, effort, and usage PlanUnits define a coherent normalization boundary across OpenCode and shared PM contracts.
items.title: Discovery and adapter data normalize through PM contracts

evidence.exact_quote: If dynamic OpenCode model discovery fails because the server is unreachable, PM must not hardcode fallback OpenCode models and instead surfaces the configured discovery error because available models depend entirely on user OpenCode configuration and authenticated providers.

items.impact: Excluding the unit from GUI work can omit the required error state; the hardcoded English sentence also lacks structured message identity, interpolation, accessibility announcement, and localization behavior.
items.statement: PO-023 sets gui_related false while requiring PM to surface a specific discovery error, and it preserves only literal English copy rather than a localizable, accessible error contract.
items.title: Discovery failure is user-visible but classified as non-GUI

evidence.exact_quote: plan mode uses the read-only OpenCode plan agent, execute mode uses the build agent

items.impact: A configured or changed OpenCode plan agent could retain mutation-capable tools while PM presents plan mode as read-only, creating a false security boundary.
items.statement: PO-024 equates mode=plan with selecting OpenCode's plan agent but does not require PM-side mutation denial, capability verification, tool-policy enforcement, or a failure oracle proving read-only behavior.
items.title: Plan mode trusts an agent label instead of enforcing read-only authority

evidence.exact_quote: OpenCode-discovered tools from GET /provider and session tool lists report through capabilities.get with category provider_tool and the shared enabled/disabled_reason/setup_hint shape so agents and users can inspect OpenCode tools through capability introspection.

items.impact: Capability and failure facts have explicit normalized consumers and media capabilities remain outside the OpenCode provider-tool surface.
items.statement: PO-025 through PO-027 normalize provider tools and failures while explicitly excluding OpenCode from PM media-generation ownership.
items.title: Provider tools, media, and failures have bounded normalization

evidence.exact_quote: OpenCode not installed. Install from https://opencode.ai
1. **Binary check:** Is `opencode` on PATH? (informational; server may be started by other means)

items.impact: An attached remote server can be healthy while Doctor tells the user to install a local binary, leading to incorrect remediation and a misleading health assessment.
items.statement: PO-028 requires the not-installed recovery message whenever OpenCode is enabled but does not condition binary severity or copy on Managed Server versus Attach to Existing Server mode, despite the source calling the binary check informational.
items.title: Doctor copy ignores attached-server mode

evidence.exact_quote: managed/attached profile creation, endpoint/auth inputs, reconnect/restart/refresh/detach actions

items.impact: Restart or detach during active or queued work can orphan requests, leak managed processes, invalidate snapshots, or misrepresent ownership without a specified guard and rollback path.
items.statement: PO-029 exposes restart and detach actions but does not define authorization, confirmation, in-flight/queued request handling, idempotency, failure rollback, or the resulting profile-state transition.
items.title: Restart and detach controls lack destructive-action contracts

evidence.exact_quote: skills/tools/runtime state separate from OpenCode-reflected server and upstream-provider state.

items.impact: The settings, tier, CLI, and retired-metadata units consistently prevent UI or compatibility surfaces from taking ownership of runtime transport and PM canon.
items.statement: PO-030 through PO-033 preserve visible ownership boundaries, shared tier layout, CLI fallback-only scope, and retirement of legacy platform_specs authority.
items.title: Settings and compatibility surfaces preserve ownership truth

evidence.exact_quote: completion, deletes the session with DELETE /session/:id, and never reuses sessions across iterations.

items.impact: Cancellation, crash, network loss, or delete failure can leave provider sessions and sensitive context behind indefinitely, while unconditional deletion can also erase the only provider-side recovery handle before PM durably settles events.
items.statement: PO-034 and PO-035 define only the successful create-send-wait-delete sequence; they omit delete-failure classification, crash recovery, startup orphan reconciliation, retention limits, deletion retry/idempotency, and the ordering between durable PM completion and provider-session deletion.
items.title: Per-iteration isolation lacks abnormal cleanup and recovery

segments.summary: Reviewed the prologue and original provider contract: transport and identity authority are strong, but concurrency is keyed to an undefined provider-account identity.
Reviewed PO-048 and the continued original contract: source-lineage boundaries are explicit, while stream retry behavior conflicts with later scheduler-owned retry rules.
Reviewed PO-002 through PO-008 plus PO-048 continuation: the atoms preserve core boundaries but their acceptance criteria validate document structure rather than provider behavior.
Reviewed PO-009 through PO-015: authority and identity boundaries are strong, but version downgrade and stale-selection execution semantics remain underspecified.
Reviewed PO-016 through PO-023: normalization boundaries are sound, but SSE ordering is contradictory and the discovery failure is misclassified as non-GUI.
Reviewed PO-024 through PO-029: capability/failure boundaries are explicit, while plan-mode enforcement, attached-profile Doctor behavior, and destructive settings actions lack operational contracts.
Reviewed PO-030 through PO-035 and the assigned context: ownership UI and compatibility boundaries are clear, but abnormal session deletion and reconciliation are unspecified.
